title: Don’t Expect Woke Hollywood to Come Roaring Back
text:

Guest Essay
Don’t Expect Woke Hollywood to Come Roaring Back
Liberal Hollywood has spent much of the past few years adapting to the MAGA vibe shift, driven by the shock waves of Donald Trump’s rise and fall and return. Was it out of touch with the country it was supposed to inform and entertain?
Now the midterms have come with a sharp pivot to the Democrats, and progressive Hollywood is dancing a jig. But given all the problems in the industry right now — from consolidation to downsizing to the looming threat of artificial intelligence — don’t expect the entertainment world to enjoy the political victory all that much.
The mood has lifted a bit — “There was a sense of relief today that maybe everything isn’t as dark as it appears,” said the producer Cathy Schulman, when asked about the midterm results — but it remains decidedly cautious.
Hollywood, in many ways, is an industry that has lost its swagger. There’s no going back to how things were before.
The Trump administration has made clear that Hollywood has to get in line with the president’s cultural and political vision. It has not been shy about using the full force of its regulatory powers, including putting a thumb on the scale in terms of whom it wanted to buy Warner Bros. Discovery.
In the process, an industry that had been, in many ways, woke, focused on telling diverse stories and becoming less of a boys’ club, became, as I wrote just last year, OK with being “hot, horny and white again.” Progress stalled on the numbers of women in positions of authority, and of people of color behind the camera and in front of it, and of L.G.B.T.Q.+ characters onscreen. In some cases, things went in reverse. According to a new GLAAD study, none of the seven trans characters from TV’s 2025-26 season are expected to return.
